codeReview.summary: The glyph-key and dirty-region updates are well scoped, but the atlas-exhaustion recovery is still incorrect when the retry path reuses cached scene replay. Clearing the native atlas invalidates previously replayable glyph coordinates, yet the second paint attempt can still replay unchanged text ranges from the prior scene instead of rerasterizing them.

issues.description: After `GlyphAtlasCache.insert` clears the atlas on exhaustion, the retry loop immediately rebuilds with the same `previousScene` and still allows `scene.replay(...)` at the cached replay sites (notably lines 196 and 446). That means any unchanged text subtree can be replayed with stale atlas UVs even though the atlas contents were wiped. In a frame that combines replayed old text with newly inserted text that triggered exhaustion, the returned `glyphAtlas` snapshot only contains glyphs reinserted after the clear, so the replayed glyph primitives can render blank or corrupted. This violates the safe-exhaustion contract for mixed replay/mutation frames.

summary: Reviewed the worker transcript skeleton, handoff, architecture/guidance files, and commit 51c682648b537e39b3d8e49cf3c34edca1eba0e9. The feature improves glyph identity and dirty-region handling, but I found one blocking correctness issue: atlas exhaustion recovery clears atlas state without invalidating scene replay, so mixed replay-plus-new-text renders can still return glyph primitives that point at cleared atlas content.
